intro: A dance in five beats surrounds a darker middle built over a persistent bass. Count two plus three, then listen for how the same metre survives changes of mood and scoring.
question: How does an unequal metre remain graceful?

cues.title: Five beats, not three
cues.text: Tchaikovsky writes this dance in 5/4. Count two beats followed by three: the unequal groups belong to the metre, not to a performer losing a waltz beat.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://en.tchaikovsky-research.net/pages/Symphony_No._6 Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_2/d450a4b450eded96239c50fdf958f258.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: A cello-led melody
cues.text: The opening tune belongs to the cellos, with light support from winds, horns and plucked strings. The melody’s long shape smooths over the unequal groups beneath it.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://en.tchaikovsky-research.net/pages/Symphony_No._6 Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_2/d450a4b450eded96239c50fdf958f258.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: Keep the unequal groups
cues.text: Try maintaining the two-plus-three pulse while following the melody. A phrase can cross the bar line without changing the underlying five-beat pattern.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://en.tchaikovsky-research.net/pages/Symphony_No._6 Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_2/d450a4b450eded96239c50fdf958f258.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: The last movement sketched
cues.text: The surviving sketches indicate that this second movement was the last of the four to be drafted. Concert order and order of composition are not the same.
cues.evidence: Historical or source-context note; no timed musical event is asserted. https://en.tchaikovsky-research.net/pages/Symphony_No._6

cues.title: The first broad crest
cues.text: The opening dance grows into a broad recorded crest before its sudden reduction. Follow the whole swell rather than treating the louder notes as a new metre.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/tchaikovsky-6-allegro-grazia.txt: The 2:15–2:25 windows are among the loudest; level drops from about −5 dB at 2:25 to −24 dB at 2:35.

cues.title: Plucked and sustained
cues.text: Pizzicato strings give an accompaniment a short release, while bowed melody and wind notes can continue across it. Listen to those contrasting lengths rather than only to the tune.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://en.tchaikovsky-research.net/pages/Symphony_No._6 Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_2/d450a4b450eded96239c50fdf958f258.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: A darker middle
cues.text: The central section moves from D major to B minor without abandoning the five-beat framework. The change of mode and accompaniment transforms the dance more than a new metre would.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://en.tchaikovsky-research.net/pages/Symphony_No._6 Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_2/d450a4b450eded96239c50fdf958f258.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: A persistent foundation
cues.text: In the middle section, repeated timpani notes help sustain a pedal beneath the melody. A pedal keeps one pitch present while the harmony above it changes.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://en.tchaikovsky-research.net/pages/Symphony_No._6 Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_2/d450a4b450eded96239c50fdf958f258.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: Grace is written down
cues.text: The heading is “Allegro con grazia” — fast, with grace. The middle section adds “con dolcezza e flebile”, asking for sweetness and a plaintive character within the same movement.
cues.evidence: Historical or source-context note; no timed musical event is asserted. https://en.tchaikovsky-research.net/pages/Symphony_No._6

cues.title: Repeated notes, changing harmony
cues.text: When the bass or percussion repeats a pitch, attend to the moving notes above it. A stationary foundation can make the upper harmony seem more unsettled rather than more secure.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://en.tchaikovsky-research.net/pages/Symphony_No._6 Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_2/d450a4b450eded96239c50fdf958f258.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: The dance returns
cues.text: The outer D-major material returns after the minor-key middle. Compare the familiar melodic contour with the darker passage that has intervened.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://en.tchaikovsky-research.net/pages/Symphony_No._6 Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_2/d450a4b450eded96239c50fdf958f258.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: A matching later crest
cues.text: The returning dance has its own strong rise and retreat. Compare its scale with the earlier swell before the minor-key middle.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/tchaikovsky-6-allegro-grazia.txt: Level reaches about −5 dB at 6:45, then falls to −22 dB by 6:55.

cues.title: Published after the premiere
cues.text: Jurgenson issued the full score in February 1894, after Tchaikovsky’s death. His own piano-duet arrangement had appeared earlier, in November 1893.
cues.evidence: Historical or source-context note; no timed musical event is asserted. https://en.tchaikovsky-research.net/pages/Symphony_No._6

cues.title: A measured departure
cues.text: Follow the closing phrases without letting the five-beat pulse become a three-beat waltz. The movement’s gentleness does not cancel the asymmetry that organised its opening.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://en.tchaikovsky-research.net/pages/Symphony_No._6 Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_2/d450a4b450eded96239c50fdf958f258.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

transitions.title: The dance turns inward
transitions.how: The outer dance relaxes after its crest. The central B-minor span retains five beats but sets a more plaintive melody above repeated D notes, including the timpani; altered mode and articulation create the contrast.
transitions.evidence: Approximate passage boundary, not a bar alignment. cache/analysis/tchaikovsky-6-allegro-grazia.txt: Strong boundaries at 2:34 and 2:40 follow the 2:20–2:25 crest; the bass estimate remains D through most of the middle. Written design: https://en.tchaikovsky-research.net/pages/Symphony_No._6 Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_2/d450a4b450eded96239c50fdf958f258.pdf

transitions.title: The outer motion returns
transitions.how: The persistent middle-section foundation gives way to the dance’s more mobile accompaniment and returning D-major melody. The five-beat metre remains unchanged; the return is articulated through texture and thematic identity.
transitions.evidence: Approximate passage boundary, not a bar alignment. cache/analysis/tchaikovsky-6-allegro-grazia.txt: A boundary at 4:54 coincides with rising onset density after the comparatively sustained middle. Written design: https://en.tchaikovsky-research.net/pages/Symphony_No._6 Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_2/d450a4b450eded96239c50fdf958f258.pdf

transitions.title: After the second crest
transitions.how: After the returning dance builds to another crest, the coda reduces its force. The score recalls the middle’s plaintive colour within the D-major close instead of ending with an unchanged full statement of the dance.
transitions.evidence: Approximate passage boundary, not a bar alignment. cache/analysis/tchaikovsky-6-allegro-grazia.txt: The 6:45 crest drops markedly by 6:55; the strongest measured boundary is 6:56, followed by a quieter closing span. Written design: https://en.tchaikovsky-research.net/pages/Symphony_No._6 Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_2/d450a4b450eded96239c50fdf958f258.pdf

timeline.note: Opening dance: cellos sing above pizzicato support; clarinets, bassoons and horns colour the phrase.
The outer dance’s later build adds trumpet punctuation to winds, horns and strings (score PDF pp. 6–7); broadly placed before the measured 2:20–2:25 crest.
Middle region: flute and violin melody above repeated D, with timpani and lower-string support.
Return region: the opening dance’s melodic and accompanimental roles recover the foreground.
The returning dance rebuilds its wind, horn and trumpet reinforcement before the report’s 6:40–6:45 crest; a broad score-proportion state.
Coda region: quieter wind phrases and strings recall the middle section’s colour before the D-major close.
Coda brass phrase: trumpets and alto/tenor trombones enter above the D foundation (score PDF p. 24); broadly placed in the 7:25–7:45 renewed closing activity.
After the brief brass phrase, the reduced ending withdraws (score PDF p. 25); the report drops markedly at 7:50. Timing is passage-level.

facts: Imperial School of Jurisprudence; Saint Petersburg Conservatory, 1862–65, with Anton Rubinstein and Nikolai Zaremba
Nadezhda von Meck supplied an allowance from 1877 to 1890; their correspondence became a major record of his working life
Six numbered symphonies and Manfred; three ballets; operas, concertos, chamber music, piano music and songs
composer.background:
Tchaikovsky was born at Votkinsk, where his father managed an ironworks. Music belonged to the household before it became a profession: his governess Fanny Dürbach remembered the child’s intense responses to it, and he began piano lessons early. His formal training nevertheless pointed towards government service. In 1850 he entered the preparatory class of the Imperial School of Jurisprudence in Saint Petersburg, separated from his family. His mother died of cholera in 1854. After graduating in 1859 he worked in the Ministry of Justice, while concerts, opera and lessons gradually occupied more of his time.

When Anton Rubinstein’s Saint Petersburg Conservatory opened in 1862, Tchaikovsky joined its first generation of students. He studied composition with Rubinstein and theoretical subjects with Nikolai Zaremba, leaving government employment in 1863. The training mattered practically: he could organise large forms, prepare orchestral scores and teach harmony. In 1866 Nikolai Rubinstein recruited him for the new Moscow Conservatory. Tchaikovsky taught there until 1878, wrote criticism and translated pedagogical material. His early reputation grew through this sustained professional work.
composer.epithet: He used the timing of dance and theatre to make a symphony’s return, interruption or collapse physically audible.
